reviewContinuity.scope: Restricted startup integration diff from 7062d4c and caused regressions, cold measurement fidelity, lifecycle/error handling, suite coverage, and the classified evaluation-history test-readiness correction. No new whole-milestone hunt.

evidenceInspected: Read AGENTS.md, REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md, regression-hunter persona, active D3 plan and success predicate, relevant Product Specification and MVP scope, Technical Decisions sections 3 and 3.1, local runtime guidance, repository PowerSync skill and JavaScript/React references. Runtime is Node v24.21.0.

Startup checks found D3 IN_PROGRESS and D3-PHONE-UPDATE NEEDS_SETUP. ci:status could not fetch the committed HEAD result; it explicitly excludes this dirty working diff. Read all regression reports 1–11, preserving FAIL rounds 1/2, prior RH-1/RH-2/RH2-1/RH2-3 dispositions and RH2-Q4. Unchanged UI fixes were not rerun.

Inspected all changed startup exports and their consumers in db.ts, migrations.ts and legacy migration harnesses; compared the worker seam with installed PowerSync 2.2.0 worker/client/options/open-factory/VFS sources and wa-sqlite 2.0.3. Seven source hashes and both package-version guards passed a direct read-only invocation.

The broker stores only promises for compiled WebAssembly.Module code, keyed by the exact same-origin WASM URL. Every dedicated open constructs a new Worker, MessageChannel and WebAssembly.Instance through a fresh stock Emscripten factory. The pinned IDBBatchAtomicVFS and SDK connection/lifetime behavior remain in place; no database, memory, connection or course state is cached.

The custom entry evaluates private worker registration before installing the stock SDK handler, and stops only the private registration message. Desktop multi-tab selection retains the SDK worker entry, module-worker mode and shared-powersync-<filename> naming. The wrapper uses the stock factory when that private worker state is absent.

Reviewed initialization memoization, error/messageerror observation, worker termination on failed initialization, compile and broker-request timeouts, rejection-cache removal and explicit reopen after failure. Successful init releases the startup watchdog. Ordered one-way DEV event and release messages drain separately from SDK readiness; diagnostics add no awaited init round trip.

Own TypeScript semantic-AST comparison proves all existing D1 spec content identical to 7062d4c after excluding only the cold-browser import and outer isolatedTest call name. The 40-student callback hash is unchanged: eb3ae347f6da6be9bddf176eb94fb40429c047b2b6947e0619040b8c496a3065. Fixture-generating statements are also AST-identical, and fixture data files are unchanged. Both 5000 ms assertions remain unchanged.

The cold-browser fixture launches the selected browser with launchOptions, headless and channel preserved, while retaining Playwright's standard context/page fixtures. The added positive case seeds the legacy file in a separate page, starts the first clock before the harness import, and requires a cache miss, compile events, two distinct workers/instances, exact 609-row equality, 40 injected students, 520 evaluations and both original bounds. No broker fetch, compile or engine construction precedes that measured import on the measured page.

The real prewarm negative control opens and closes a database before measurement, clears only telemetry, observes cache-hit rather than cache-miss, and requires the cold-evidence validator to reject it. Both controls check independent writes, close/reopen, IDB deletion and reset without retaining old rows.

Read corrected prototype CI evidence for ca889d3 / run 38632601491: four strict cold/control cases and 22 original migration/read-only cases passed with zero flakes/skips; WebKit measured 1256/427 ms, identical 609 rows and cold-miss/fresh-instance telemetry. It is explicitly diagnostic evidence, not exact production-integration acceptance.

Read the preserved broad-route failure report: four initial failures faulted Vite's WASM URL-module response before binary compilation. The corrected route targets only the engine binary and requires cache-miss/compile-start before interruption. The failed report remains preserved; it was not relabeled PASS.

Read the OS-temp startup-safety recovery report (SHA256 89453f585f22ac66c7acad8cfd42bc4cd9a047fd303b2f59d33eae65c1a23dc0): 12 first-attempt passes, zero unexpected/skipped/flaky results. Chromium and WebKit cover blocked-fetch page closure, held-write rollback, corrupt compile plus explicit reopen, structured-clone fallback excluded from cold evidence, lost broker port and crashed worker. Recovery preserves identical 609 rows and permits later IDB deletion.

Read the OS-temp startup-safety multitab report (SHA256 2d0d350ea3ae18cb9fc68d52ea1cfaf4e6510c60801fb311658b9c2c000b3b5a): one real desktop Chromium two-page test passed, retries 0. The surviving page writes after another closes; a newer claim blocks an already-open older writer; a newly opened older app remains read-only and leaves needed repairs unapplied; final IDB deletion succeeds.

Compared scratch sources with this working tree. Startup broker, entry, registration, schema, harness and multitab spec match. The factory differs only in replacing the initialized timeout variable/conditional clear with a const assigned before postMessage; all cleanup callers run after that assignment. The recovery-spec difference is formatting. The reports are not claimed to be exact full-source CI.

Directly read test-results/d3-ready-deadline/report.json, SHA256 486320943ed03f721b38179de8527b1c7658ce31f704cb1795216eab75b68212. The current integration's real 31-second readiness-watchdog crossing passed on Pixel Chromium (38009 ms) and iPhone WebKit (39421 ms), retries 0, with post-deadline write, close, fresh reopen and deletion. Repeated init creates only one instance.

Normal coverage adds desktop-chrome-storage for the new SharedWorker test; Pixel excludes only that new desktop-specific spec. WebKit gains startup and recovery specs, the D3 focus manifest adds all three new specs, and Linux CI includes desktop storage. Existing project membership, assertion bounds, retries and skips are unchanged. The runner forwards project arguments and manifest focus entries.

The quick run's 1361/1362 result is preserved in .evidence/D3/evaluation-history-readiness.json. Persistence is mocked in the one failed history case; the named region exists during its loader. The unchanged test file passed 3/3 in classification. Reviewed exactly three getByRole-to-awaited-findByRole changes for the existing first loaded button, heading and error. All original assertions and default waits remain; application evaluation source is unchanged. Fresh final verification is pending.

Confirmed summary component, image renderer, share implementation and summary-image assertion helper are unchanged from 7062d4c. git diff --check passed. Root reported the shared production build passing. This reviewer launched no browser or test suite, made no tracked edits and saved this report as OS-temp cvc-d3-regression-round12.json.
